newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision prepares for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision prepares for privatisation.

text.p: The board of Spanish telecommunications group Retevision will meet next week to convert itself into a limited company -- a first step toward the forthcoming privatisation of up to 80 percent of its capital, a spokesman said on Friday.
"The board of Retevision will meet next week to approve the asset valuation of its auditors and contribution to the limited company," the spokesman told Reuters.
He added that the valuation would be a decisive factor in setting the share price for the privatisation.

The Spanish government is seen approving the privatisation framework for the 100-percent state-owned company in the coming weeks, after which the stake sale would take place in not much more than three months.
Retevision, Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica de Espana, is due to be fully privatised by 2000 and many domestic and foreign groups have said they are interested.
Among the domestic firms Banco Santander, Banco Central Hispano and Endesa are interested.
Among international groups, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom could bid jointly for a stake of between 25 and 30 percent of Retevision.
Others tipped to be interested in buying shares are British Telecommunications, Cable & Wireless and the Italian Stet.
Retevision's turnover in 1995 was 32 billion pesetas.
